column1: # WHAT THIS IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. One row per thing the normative specification
# (language-spec.md Part I, N1-N14) requires, plus the one feature-list item kept
# in 1.0 (C FFI). It is the ENUMERATION. It is deliberately NOT the gate.
# 1.0 IS `make thesis-exit`: bootstrap/pdc.pd rewritten in the differentiated
# dialect — ref/ref mut with inferred regions, a discharged #[total], inferred
# effects and no async/await — still reaching a byte-identical stage1/stage2
# fixed point, with a second witness program meeting the same conditions.
# WHAT `satisfied` MEANS, AND THE QUESTION THAT CATCHES A ROW WHOSE TRUTH IS
# CONDITIONAL. `satisfied` means WITNESSED BY THE CITED EVIDENCE — an instance —
# never "holds for every program". The useful test on any row is not "is this true
# today" but: WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE OF THE PROGRAM UNDER TEST, AND DOES THIS
# ROW SAY IT? A row that survives only because no witness exercises an excluded
# feature has the same defect as one that is simply wrong, and it is harder to see.
# The instance that produced this paragraph: SH-01's byte-identical fixed point is
# green because PBS-1 excludes BOTH imports and generics, and there are two
# independent unordered emission sources — one per exclusion, separated by
# measurement, not inference. The row asserted the property and stated neither
# condition. It states both now, and SH-05 carries both obligations.
# WHY NOT "the inventory has no unmet rows". Because that is a COMPLETENESS
# criterion, and completeness criteria are what this repository spent M1 burning
# line on an inventory and the same disease returns under a new name. A vacuous
# fixture can print "unimplemented" and PASS; a compiler cannot compile itself
# vacuously. The fixed point is the one artifact here that structurally cannot
# lie, so it is what the definition rests on, and scope follows from what the
# compiler actually uses rather than from argument.
# WHY THE ENUMERATION STILL EXISTS. So that nothing is dropped silently. A
# requirement the thesis does not exercise is marked `post-1.0` HERE, in writing,
# with an owner — it is not deleted, and it is not quietly absent. The previous
# draft of this file made the enumeration the gate; that criterion went green
# with all three differentiators unimplemented, because N7/N8/N9 anchor no rows
# in feature-index.toml precisely BECAUSE they are unimplemented.
# CLOSED, in the same sense as tests/conformance-manifest.txt:
#   - Every row needs an owner, an evidence kind, an evidence locator and a
#   - A `satisfied` row whose evidence stops resolving turns the gate RED. That
#     is what stops the debt inventories from shrinking by deletion: an
#     `#[ignore]` test can be deleted and cargo's list simply gets shorter, but
#     a row here that names it fails.
#   - Deleting a row, moving it between milestones, or moving it to `post-1.0`
#     is a CONTRACT TRANSITION and is reviewed as one.
#   - RECONCILIATION, both directions. Every red row in either debt inventory
#     must map to a row here, and every `owed` row here must name evidence that
#         tests/conformance-manifest.txt must appear in the evidence column of at
#         least one row here. That is checkable today, by path.
#       * Rust tests: every #[ignore = "XFAIL: ..."] must carry a requirement id
#         — `req: N5-06` — and that id must exist here. THIS DOES NOT HOLD YET:
#         the reasons carry a milestone, not a requirement, so today's
#         reconciliation of that inventory is by review, not by command. Adding
#         the id is an edit to tests/ and lands with F9's re-tagging.
# COLUMNS (TAB-separated, all NINE mandatory, `-` for N/A):
#   id  milestone  source  requirement  evidence-kind  evidence  status  disposition
#   fixture     a conformance row of class `run` with a recorded transcript.
#               POSITIVE evidence: the construct is accepted AND produces the
#               right answer. stdout is the runtime observable.
#   reject      a conformance row of class `reject`. NEGATIVE evidence: the
#               compiler must refuse it with the declared diagnostic. FOR AN
#               INFERENCE FEATURE THE REJECTION IS THE PRODUCT — a region
#               inferencer that accepts everything is a no-op, and a no-op
#               disguises itself perfectly as green fixtures. That is exactly
#   skip        a conformance row of class `skip`, proven so by the compiler.
#   observable  a Rust integration test asserting a runtime property stdout
#               cannot show — wall-clock overlap, process exit status, the
#               structure of the generated C, a linked symbol.
#   gate        a make target that must exit 0.
#   decision    an owner decision that must be recorded before the row can be
#               written at all. A `blocked` row is not work; it is a question.
#   satisfied   the evidence exists and is green TODAY (2026-08-22, 7484bac).
#   owed        the evidence does not exist or does not pass.
#   blocked     cannot be specified until the named decision is made.
#   thesis      `make thesis-exit` reads this row directly. These rows ARE the
#   1.0         in 1.0: the witnesses exercise it, or the thesis rows rest on it.
#   post-1.0    enumerated and explicitly deferred, owner `P1`. Recorded rather
#               than dropped, so the omission cannot become the next generation's
# fingerprint: for a `reject` row, the diagnostic the refusal MUST carry; `-` otherwise.
#   A rejection is not evidence of a language property unless it is the INTENDED
#   rejection. "Refused because the prohibition is enforced" and "refused for
#   incidental unsupported syntax" are the same verdict to a runner that only sees
#   REJECTED — and a sibling branch can turn a reject fixture green with no compiler
#   change at all. So a thesis reject row NAMES the fingerprint, and the corpus row for
#   that fixture must declare it; scripts/conformance.sh has already matched the
#   declared fingerprint against the actual diagnostic.
# A milestone's exit is: no row owned by it is `owed` or `blocked`, and the
# reconciliation above holds. 1.0's exit is `make thesis-exit`.
# N14-17 WAS ADDED 2026-08-23, and an added row is a contract transition like any
# other. Its evidence is `make stdlib-gate` and NOT a fixture: the row says EVERY
# normative builtin is callable, and a single driver spans a few of them. The gate
# holds the whole-registry invariant — Phase 3 requires the manifest's name set to
# equal the registry's, that no row is UNUSABLE, and that `reconcile` finds no
# `Support::Unsupported` entry at all. Evidence has to be as wide as the claim; the
# first version of this row cited `tests/stdlib/stdlib_builtins_file.pd`, which
# exercises the file family while the string and char/argument families are covered
# by other drivers entirely. MILESTONES.md's M2 item 6 DECLARED that `file_flush` and `file_seek` get
# re-based and that the four `*_ex` wrappers go, and no row of this manifest said
# so — which meant the M2 filter could have reached zero-owed with both builtins
# still uncallable and four dead wrappers still emitted into every program. That
# is the unowned-requirement hole this inventory exists to close, reproduced
# inside it. The work is done and the row records the obligation rather than the
# achievement: it goes red the moment any normative builtin is registered and
# refused again. `N14-01` is about the NAME SET and could not have caught it;
# `N14-03` is about SIGNATURES and belongs to M3.
# id  milestone  source  requirement  evidence-kind  evidence  status  disposition

column1: # --- Self-hosting: the project's own claim about pdc -------------------------------------

column4: bootstrap/pdc.pd compiles itself to a byte-identical fixed point over PBS-1 - MEASURED UNDER TWO EXCLUSIONS THIS ROW NOW STATES, NOT ONE: the unit imports NOTHING (grep -c '^import' bootstrap/pdc.pd = 0) and uses NO GENERICS (grep -cE 'fn [a-zA-Z_]+<' bootstrap/pdc.pd = 0; docs/specification/bootstrap-subset.md:76 excludes them from PBS-1), and pdc.pd:8 states the exclusion as a virtue - 'This file is written in exactly the subset it implements'. So THIS ROW IS EVIDENCE THAT PBS-1 AVOIDS BOTH UNORDERED EMISSION SOURCES, NOT THAT THE COMPILER IS DETERMINISTIC. Byte identity for a unit that imports OR is generic is SH-05

Module emission AND generic-instantiation emission are ORDER-DETERMINISTIC, so the fixed point survives the rewrite. TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES, SEPARATED BY MEASUREMENT AND NOT BY INFERENCE. (a) MODULES: imported modules live in a HashMap (src/codegen/mod.rs:81) emitted by iterating .values() (src/codegen/mod.rs:1140, :1193, :1278); measured, 8 compiles of one unchanged two-module program produced 2 distinct SHA-1s, 4 each - a pure ordering swap of two function bodies. (b) GENERICS: instantiations live in HashMaps (src/typeck/mod.rs:321, :329) emitted by iterating .keys() (src/typeck/mod.rs:2931, :2948) and consumed at src/codegen/mod.rs:1316, :1774; measured, six generics with ZERO imports produced 30 distinct outputs in 30 compiles - generics alone break byte-stability with no module in sight, and six modules with no generics was byte-identical. NEITHER HALF DISCHARGES THE OTHER: ordering the module iteration leaves (b) standing, and ordering the instantiation iteration leaves (a) standing. NEITHER IS A DEFECT REPORT FILED AGAINST SOMEONE ELSE: repairing a mechanism retires no part of this row, because the requirement is that byte identity survive the REWRITE of pdc.pd into the differentiated dialect, which uses imports and generics both. This row is satisfied only by a rewritten unit that exercises both and still reaches the fixed point
bootstrap/pdc.pd compiles EVERY fixture in the conformance corpus
Its output matches the Rust compiler's on every fixture, acceptances and refusals alike
PBS-1 is the whole 1.0 language, not a subset
